operational-example.copy: Use Movement Row for one transaction record: category icon, merchant/context, signed amount, and visible status. Receipt detail, support, dispute, export, and grouped timelines remain patterns.

scenario.title: Movement Row
scenario.meta: ZIP TransactionRow parity governed by Flow: category icon, title/meta stack, amount column, and status text.
rationale: The ZIP TransactionRow is a list row, not a pill button; Flow now follows that anatomy.
Category color is support only; title, meta, signed amount, and status stay visible as text.
Movement detail, support, dispute, export, and day grouping escalate to patterns.

items.rule: One tappable or readable movement record.
Date, station, vehicle, or card context.
Shows value and approval state with text.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, error, pending, focus, hover, default
items: Provide a visible accessible label for the component.
Expose status and state in text, not color alone.
Keep keyboard focus and touch targets predictable.
Protect sensitive or operational data from overexposure.
Escalate to a pattern when actions, grouping, or detail flows exceed one component.

variants.copy: Movement Row variants adjust transaction type and density; movement detail and support flows remain patterns.

states.copy: Movement Row states communicate hover, focus, pending, error, and disabled behavior for one record. Completed transactions do not need an extra approved label.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant controls transaction emphasis; state controls processing or risk without adding detail system behavior.

full-width.copy: Movement Row can fill list containers and sheets while keeping each row to one record.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: On phones, stack amount below content when needed; do not hide status or amount.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport rules protect scanability for one record and do not create grouped timeline behavior.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use touch-safe targets and preserve key text.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the component close to its related card or movement context.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density only when scanability remains intact.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify title, metadata, amount, status, variant, and state for one movement.

api-foundations.copy: Movement Row API exposes label, meta, amount, status, icon, variant, and state while Design System owns row geometry, focus, and state precedence.

props.name: category
props.type: fuel | charge | toll | food | transfer | income

props.name: state
props.type: default | hover | focus | pending | error | disabled

groups.title: Use
items: Use metadata for source and context.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not include receipt detail inside the row.
Do not make rows depend on color-only status.
Do not group timelines inside the component.

groups.title: Review
items: Check amount alignment and tabular numerals.

rejectIf: Support, dispute, or export actions live inside the component.
Amount or status disappears on mobile.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Movement Row as one list record. Agents may place it inside movement lists, while humans confirm status language, amount formatting, and whether detail/support behavior belongs to a pattern.
canDecide: Use Movement Row for card activity, fuel purchases, refunds, declined movements, and pending transactions.
Keep the row to one record with one amount and one visible status.
Use compact variant in dense mobile sheets when amount remains visible.
mustAsk: The user needs receipt detail, dispute, export, support, or audit history.
Amount formatting, currency, or source status is unclear.
Rows need grouping, sticky dates, or timeline orchestration.
rejectIf: Support, dispute, or export actions live inside the component.
Amount or status disappears on mobile.
miel.handoff: I am using Movement Row for one transaction record. Please confirm amount format, status copy, metadata, tap target behavior, and whether detail/support belongs to a movement-detail pattern.
